rationale: The application only passes a proxy option with auth to axios. The leak originates two repositories down, in follow-redirects. At tag v1.15.4, the redirect handler in index.js strips confidential headers on a cross-host / less-secure redirect with `removeMatchingHeaders(/^(?:authorization|cookie)$/i, this._options.headers)` — the Proxy-Authorization header is not in that set, so it survives a cross-host redirect. The real upstream fix (follow-redirects commit c4f847f85176991f95ab9c88af63b1294de8649b, released in 1.15.6) widens the pattern to `/^(?:(?:proxy-)?authorization|cookie)$/i`. axios's Node HTTP adapter (lib/adapters/http.js) synthesizes the Proxy-Authorization header from the proxy option in its setProxy helper and, when redirects are enabled, substitutes follow-redirects (httpFollow/httpsFollow) as the transport in place of the raw Node http/https module; axios's dispatch layer (lib/core/dispatchRequest.js) selects that adapter at request time. The transport substitution is a runtime assignment, not an import an application-level import graph reveals, which is why the leaking line lives in a repo the developer never named.

required_files.rationale: Fix site: the cross-host redirect branch strips only /^(?:authorization|cookie)$/i at v1.15.4, omitting Proxy-Authorization, so proxy credentials leak. Real upstream fix (commit c4f847f85176) adds (?:proxy-)? to the stripped pattern.

The Node HTTP adapter's setProxy helper synthesizes the Proxy-Authorization header from the proxy option and substitutes follow-redirects as the transport; the hop that carries the credential header into the leaking library.
The request-dispatch layer that selects the configured adapter at request time; the entry into the adapter chain an investigator traverses to reach the transport substitution.
